entities.summary: Natalis was Archbishop of Milan in the mid-8th century, playing a significant role in the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches. He was instrumental in shaping the theological and ecclesiastical landscape of the Mediterranean region during this period. Natalis's leadership and influence extended beyond his immediate context, contributing to the ongoing debates about the nature of Christ and the role of the Church in society. Through his writings and teachings, Natalis helped to establish the foundations for the development of Christian liturgy and devotional practices. As a prominent figure in the early Middle Ages, Natalis's legacy continues to be felt in the modern-day practices and traditions of the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches. His feast day, May 13, remains a cherished occasion for the faithful, commemorating his life, teachings, and devotion to Christ.
